question: Should existing GitHub-backed skills with already-stored over-limit display names be preserved on sync, or intentionally normalized to the new 40-character limit?
rationale: This PR adds a new public metadata policy and can rewrite existing stored catalog rows; source inspection cannot infer the intended upgrade behavior.

options.title: Preserve GitHub-backed legacy names
options.body: Keep unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names grandfathered like hosted titles, then enforce the limit only for new or renamed values.

options.title: Accept sync normalization
options.body: Allow next sync to shorten existing GitHub-backed names, but require the PR to state and test that upgrade behavior explicitly.

options.title: Pause for policy
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers confirm both the 40-character maximum and hosted-versus-GitHub legacy handling.

recommendation.title: Preserve GitHub-backed legacy names
recommendation.body: Keep unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names grandfathered like hosted titles, then enforce the limit only for new or renamed values.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest owner signal for the current publish and GitHub-backed sync paths and is also requested for review on the PR.
